# Regular canonical pairing under the specified C16 action

This package supports the LP regular-pairing proposition in the manuscript.
It distinguishes three things: the support-enumeration algorithm, preserved
completed executions, and small certificates whose finite consequences can be
checked independently. The executions are **not formal proof objects**. The
quick checker cannot establish that a physical-word pool is exhaustive; that
premise rests on the released search, the completeness argument below, and its
completed execution records.

| Input | Code | Search cap | Pure Z orbits | Minimum nontrivial X/Z support union | Pair vertices | Proper colors | Regular canonical width |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| LPQ6 (Q6) | [[1088,128,16]], check weight 9 | 17 | 45 | 26 | 177 | 5 | 18 exactly |
| LPQ5 (Q5) | [[1088,128,20]], check weight 10 | 20 | 75 | 32 | 88 | 3 | between 21 and 22 |

Both sectors separately have regular bases of maximum weight equal to the
distance; their explicit seeds are in `data/*_sector_bases.json` and their full logical ranks are checked here. The lower
bounds above concern **any canonical frame organized into the specified cyclic
orbits**, not a single selected frame. The exclusions also allow mixed Pauli
seeds. They do not establish unrestricted canonical width above distance.
For Q6 the unrestricted width is either 16 or 18; for Q5 this package proves no
unrestricted lower bound beyond 20.

## Quick independent checks

From the repository root, with Python 3.10 or later and no third-party packages:

```sh
python3 verification/regular_pairing/check.py
```

The script checks CSS commutation and ranks; the specified translation and
sector-exchange symmetries; canonical frame pairing; the search input's check
row space and complete logical detector space; syndromes and nontriviality of
every translated pool word; minimal-mask orbit normalization; logical-class
coordinates; every pairing-polynomial coefficient; every relative-shift support
union; all compatibility-graph vertices and edges; and the actual proper color
assignment. It also binds the normalized pools to both recorded and fresh
complete execution transcripts by input/source hashes and output comparison.

## Replay the exhaustive searches

A C++17 compiler is additionally required. Choose a new output directory;
the runner refuses to replace existing execution records.

```sh
python3 verification/regular_pairing/replay.py --code LPQ6 --output /tmp/pairing-replay --compiler c++ --seconds 1800
python3 verification/regular_pairing/replay.py --code LPQ5 --output /tmp/pairing-replay --compiler c++ --seconds 3600
```

The runner compiles a temporary binary with `-O3 -std=c++17`, runs all 68 root
blocks without child or modular partitioning, preserves stdout/stderr and
compiler flags, elapsed runtimes, and hashes, and compares every normalized output
orbit with the released pool. `TIMEOUT`, an external interruption, a nonzero
return code, a missing completion marker, or a different pool fails the replay.
A partial run is not a nonexistence certificate. The executables are deleted
after the run; no binary or per-node trace is needed in the repository.

`src/kernel_minima_reverse.cpp` and `src/kernel_minima_native.cpp` are the
byte-identical programs used in the original Q6 and Q5 enumerations. The former
reverses the candidate branch order. Their original header describes the parent
distance-exclusion implementation; the actual `WORD`/`ENUMERATION_COMPLETE`
output behavior is the enumeration version. The unused success-stop state never
interrupts enumeration. The publication wrapper exposes only an unpartitioned
replay, although the preserved engines also contain the original partition
options.

### The important Q6 pruning switch

For Q6, `inputs/LPQ6.txt` has **zero stabilizer rows in its second group** (`rZ=0`).
Thus every `col_stabs[j]` is empty and `overlap_ok(j)` always returns true.
Stabilizer-overlap pruning is disabled, for the root and every later branch.
Both the quick checker and replay metadata verify/record this condition.
Deleting only a command-line option would not suffice: the input controls it.
Q5 retains the stabilizer rows because its search cap is the certified distance,
at which the strict half-overlap rule cannot discard a minimum logical word.

## Why this enumerates the required pools

1. Binary coordinates are `(2*quaternary_block + trace_component)*16 + position`,
   using trace basis `(omega,omega^2)`. The group generator increments `position`
   within each binary block. Translating any support sends one occupied position
   in its first occupied block to zero. Roots `b*16`, with all earlier blocks
   forbidden, therefore cover every translation orbit.
2. At a node, an unsatisfied check must meet the remaining support an odd number
   of times. Branches select its first available neighbor and forbid earlier
   choices. Every allowed extension follows one of these branches. The choice
   of check or branch order affects runtime, not coverage.
3. Syndrome-weight and disjoint-neighborhood bounds are necessary conditions on
   any completion within the remaining weight budget. The optional strict
   stabilizer half-overlap rule preserves every minimum logical word: a removed
   candidate would be shortened by that stabilizer without changing its class.
4. A zero-syndrome node is tested against a complete X-logical detector basis;
   nonzero logical syndrome identifies a nontrivial Z class. The search then
   stops that branch, so it enumerates irreducible supports rather than arbitrary
   unions of disjoint kernel words. Every minimum nontrivial logical is
   irreducible. Consequently, the smallest output weight gives the distance
   when the run completes (16 for Q6, 20 for Q5).
5. For Q5 the cap equals that minimum. For Q6 every nonzero kernel word has
   weight at least two because every column of H_X is nonzero. A logical of
   weight at most 17 cannot split into a nontrivial component of weight at least
   16 and another nonzero kernel component. All such logicals are therefore
   irreducible. With overlap pruning disabled, all representatives through 17
   are retained. All 45 Q6 orbits found have weight 16; all 75 Q5 orbits have
   weight 20.

The code parser and finite checker verify the relevant ranks, detector span,
translation symmetry, and absence of zero columns. The argument still relies on
the correctness of the exhaustive implementation and execution environment; a
compact independently checked coloring certifies only the graph conclusion.

## From physical pools to the width bounds

`data/*_pool.json` contains sorted physical supports. The normalized representative
is the smallest integer mask among all 16 translates, with bit q denoting physical
coordinate q. The X pool is the tensor-transpose image of the Z pool; this order
is retained, rather than independently renormalizing or reordering the X pool.

`data/*_certificate.json` contains the hexadecimal physical masks, logical-class
coordinates for all 16 translates, the complete pairing-polynomial matrix,
the orbit-pair support-union minima, every monomial-pair vertex, graph adjacency
lists, and a proper coloring. Logical coordinates are pairings with the opposite
sector of the canonical frame in `*_physical.json`; its index is
`16*seed + translation`. Coefficient bit h of a pairing polynomial is
`<x_i,t^h z_j>`. A pair vertex `(i,j,h)` means this polynomial is exactly `t^h`.

The support-union calculation is

```
min over i,j and h=0,...,15 of |supp(x_i) union supp(t^h z_j)|.
```

There are 32,400 tested relative unions for Q6 and 90,000 for Q5. A simultaneous
translation of both supports preserves their union size, so this covers all
relative physical placements. The minima 26 and 32 exceed the respective caps.
Thus a sufficiently low-weight mixed operator has at most one nontrivial CSS
component. Removing a stabilizer component does not increase weight or change
logical pairings. Because the group action preserves each CSS sector, one can
purify a seed first and then translate it throughout its orbit.

Two monomial-pair vertices are adjacent precisely when both cross-pairing
polynomials vanish. A full regular canonical frame would require eight mutually
compatible vertices, since k/P=8. The released 5- and 3-color proper colorings
exclude an eight-clique. **Color optimality is neither claimed nor needed.**
The original canonical frames, checked directly, give upper widths 18 and 22.
For Q6 the complete pure pool through 17 contains only weight-16 representatives,
so a width-17 unrestricted frame would purify to width 16; no width-17 optimum
is possible. Existence of an unrestricted width-16 frame remains unresolved.

`build_certificates.py` regenerates the finite certificate files from the stored
physical pools. It does not establish completeness. Polynomial construction
uses translated dot products, whereas `check.py` verifies those coefficients
by physical within-block position differences.

## Evidence and costs

`records/records/` and `records/replay/` contain metadata-normalized execution
records. File hashes bind the public copies. The records include input, source,
executable and transcript fingerprints, compiler flags, elapsed wall time,
user and system CPU time, and final node counts. Each search
process is single-threaded; wall times are measurements, not isolated benchmark
guarantees. No billions-of-nodes dump is stored.

Recorded runs visited 56,921,793 nodes in 37.0 s (Q6) and 574,585,503 nodes in
450.1 s (Q5). The packaged replays used `-O3 -std=c++17`; their JSON
receipts report the measured elapsed costs. Hardware and software-version
metadata are omitted, so these timings are not reproducible benchmark claims.

Public receipts have calendar, job, and workstation metadata removed. File hashes
bind the normalized copies. Executable fingerprints are declarations; compiled
binaries are omitted. Portable replay builds from the supplied source.

content.logical_coordinate_convention: Bit i is pairing with canonical opposite-sector frame operator i. Index i = 16*seed + translate.
content.polynomial_convention: Bit h is <x_i,t^h z_j>; coefficients in F2 and h=0,...,15.
content.union_convention: Entry (i,j) is min over ALL h=0,...,15 of |supp(x_i) union supp(t^h z_j)|. A common translation preserves weight.
content.vertex_convention: Lexicographic triples (i,j,h) such that G_ij=t^h; normalize the canonical pair by a relative translation.
content.coloring_method: DSATUR: maximum distinct neighbor colors, then larger degree, then smaller vertex index; use smallest available nonnegative color.

content.balancing_operation_codes: 0=first raw row;1=second raw row;2=sum; choose two smallest(weight,operation_code) at translate0, identically for every translate
